# OTR Newsletter #3: Shaping the Open Transition: OTR Symposium Info session on 9 June

We've reached another milestone for Open Technology Research (OTR).

This week, OTR [published](https://opentechresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Open-Technology-Research-A-Shared-Research-Agenda.pdf) its shared research agenda – a deliberately open draft that names the most critical gaps in how we understand, measure, and sustain open technologies – and launched the official [Call for Proposals](https://pretalx.com/otrsymposium2026/cfp) for the [OTR Symposium 2026](https://symposium.opentechresearch.org/), taking place 26–27 October at the [University of Barcelona](https://web.ub.edu/en/). We're also welcoming the [Digital Infrastructure Insights Fund](https://infrastructureinsights.fund/) (D//F) as a full partner, bringing a rich body of funded research and implementation insight that directly advances what OTR is trying to build.

The research agenda reflects what we heard consistently across our global consultations: that the evidence base for open technology investment, regulation, and adoption remains fragmented, underfunded, and skewed toward a small number of high-income countries. It identifies the questions that matter most; for example, how to measure economic value in terms that reach procurement officers and budget units, how hybrid governance models are functioning in practice, what makes open technology deployment durable rather than reversible, and how we sustain the maintainers and communities that underpin infrastructure the rest of the world depends on. It is a draft because we want you to push back on it.

The OTR Symposium 2026 theme – Shaping the Open Transition – reflects a deliberate shift in emphasis: from mapping problems to asking what it will take to go further. Keynotes will be anchored in what is already working. Sessions will be designed to connect research directly to policy and practice. The goal is not to present conclusions already reached, but to function as a genuine working session that sharpens priorities, surfaces the most urgent research designs, and strengthens the cross-border connections this field currently lacks.

If you're working at the intersection of open technology and governance, economics, sustainability, security, AI, or digital sovereignty, we want to hear from you. [Submit](https://pretalx.com/otrsymposium2026/cfp) to the CFP before 5 July.

And if you'd like to learn more or connect with the OTR community before you do, [join one of our upcoming open info sessions](https://opentechresearch.org/blog/got-questions-about-the-otr-symposium-2026-join-our-info-sessions-on-9-june/).

## New Open Technologies News

**Open-source AI hardware could weaken Big Tech’s grip on AI (March 2026)** – Current AI, a $400 million public-interest initiative, has unveiled an open source, offline AI device built with India's Bhashini project that runs locally on limited hardware and supports 22 Indic languages – designed as a direct alternative to cloud-dependent Big Tech AI. It's a concrete example of the “frugal AI” argument: that the drive for ever-larger models serves only part of the world, and that open, portable, locally-run systems may better serve the rest. → [Read more](https://restofworld.org/2026/current-ai-bhashini-open-source-handheld-device-2/)

**United Nations launches Open Source United Portal (April 2026)**– The United Nations has launched the Open Source United (OSU) portal as a central point of reference for open source activity across the UN system. → [Read more](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/open-source-observatory-osor/news/united-nations-launches-open-source-united-portal)

**Aligning Research and Innovation Funding to the Dynamics of Digital Commons (April 2026)** – The EU's research funding architecture was built for short-term, market-driven innovation – not the maintenance and governance work that keeps open source infrastructure alive, leaving critical Digital Commons chronically underfunded. This brief from Open Future proposes a layered fix: sustained core funding for foundational open source (along the lines of an EU Sovereign Tech Fund) paired with tiered pathways to help successful commons initiatives scale beyond the pilot stage. → [Read more](https://openfuture.eu/publication/aligning-research-and-innovation-funding-to-the-dynamics-of-digital-commons/)

**Open Source Organizations Weigh in on Age Attestation in the U.S. (May 2026)**– The Open Source Initiative (OSI), Apereo Foundation, FreeBSD Foundation, and Open Source Technology Improvement Fund (OSTIF) issued a statement asking policymakers in the U.S. to engage with the Open Source community when considering age attestation requirements for operating systems. → [Read more](https://opensource.org/?p=411160)

**Commission hails full-stack tech sovereignty approach, document reveals (May 2026)**– The European Commission is soon expected to release its new Tech Sovereignty Package, including significant new developments on open source, cloud services, AI, and chips. The Commission’s proposed Open Source Strategy is still present, albeit as a subset of a larger communication outlining the package’s vision for European technological sovereignty. → [Read more](https://www.euractiv.com/news/commission-hails-full-stack-tech-sovereignty-approach-document-reveals/)

**Hackers have compromised dozens of popular open source packages in an ongoing supply-chain attack (May 2026)** – A coordinated supply-chain attack hijacked hundreds of npm packages in minutes by compromising developer accounts, with victims including OpenAI. The incidents show that open source is inherently less secure, but because its scale means a single breach cascades fast in the AI era. It's an argument not against openness, but for stronger platform-level protections to match the trust the world places in shared code. → [Read more](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/19/hackers-have-compromised-dozens-of-popular-open-source-packages-in-an-ongoing-supply-chain-attack/)

**IBM and Red Hat Commit $5 Billion to Redefine the Future of Open Source in the AI Era (May 2026)**– IBM and Red Hat have announced Project Lightwell, a $5 billion initiative deploying 20,000 engineers and AI tooling to create a trusted security clearinghouse for enterprise open source — covering vulnerability detection, validated patching, and responsible upstream disclosure. It's a significant bet that securing open source at scale requires both human expertise and AI capacity working together, not trading one off against the other. → [Read more](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-05-28-ibm-and-red-hat-commit-5-billion-to-redefine-the-future-of-open-source-in-the-ai-era)

**Global Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) Summit heads to Indonesia in 2027 (May 2026)**– The Global DPI Summit heads to Bali in March 2027 – its first Asian edition – reflecting both Indonesia's growing DPI leadership and the expanding global momentum behind foundational digital systems now active in over 100 countries. It's a timely venue as debates intensify over whether DPI is built on open, reusable, interoperable foundations or becomes another layer of proprietary lock-in. → [Read more](https://www.undp.org/digital-innovation/press-releases/global-digital-public-infrastructure-dpi-summit-heads-indonesia-2027)

**Open-Source Software for Public Practitioners (May 2026)**– A UNDP-backed primer on open source software makes the case for OSS adoption in Small Island Developing States, using Trinidad and Tobago's new Open Source Programme Office as a lead example. The core argument is practical as much as philosophical: for governments with limited budgets and a need for adaptable, interoperable digital infrastructure, open source isn't just a cost-saving measure but a sovereignty strategy. → [Read more](https://www.undp.org/trinidad-and-tobago/blog/open-source-software-public-practitioners)

## New Open Technologies Reports and Research

### Assessing Age Assurance Technologies: Effectiveness, Side-Effects, and Acceptance (March 26, 2026)

This paper provides an overview and evaluation of different types of age assurance technologies (AAT). It describes and analyzes: 1) different approaches to age assurance online (age verification, age estimation, age inference, and parental control and consent), as well as 2) different age assurance architectures (online, offline device-based, offline credential-based), and assesses their various combinations with regard to their respective a) effectiveness, b) side effects, and c) acceptance. → [Read more](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.25695)

### Open for debate: governance, power, and the limits of internet openness (April 2026)

This volume is an edited collection examining how “internet openness” has shifted from a technical ideal rooted in open protocols to a contested political and economic condition shaped by states, corporations, and competing regulatory regimes. The core question at its heart is no longer whether the internet is open in principle, but who gets to define openness, and who bears the cost when they do. → [Read more](https://cadmus.eui.eu/entities/publication/a8189891-83f0-43d3-812e-37340cc063a5?ref=internet.exchangepoint.tech)

### Impact of global technological turn and innovations for humanitarian aid and development: A systematic review on the pathways to sustainable development (1 April 2026)

This study investigates how humanitarian technologies (HT) are reshaping pathways to sustainable development (SD) worldwide. It explores the critical intersection of humanitarian technology, existing sustainability frameworks, and global equity by emphasizing the transformative potential of innovations to advance human and planetary wellbeing. Using PRISMA guidelines, the study systematically assesses how humanity-based technologies have contributed to achieving the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) between 2015 and 2024, while identifying trends, disparities, and policy implications that influence global sustainability outcomes. → [Read more](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2590291126003086)

### Beyond Adoption: Examining the Evolution and Impact of Codes of Conduct on Open-Source Communities (15 April 2026)

Research tracking Codes of Conduct across thousands of GitHub projects finds that adopting one reliably attracts new contributors over time – a meaningful signal for open source community health. The catch: existing contributors disengage more in the short term, suggesting CoCs shift community culture in ways that reward inclusion but require careful change management. → [Read more](https://ftw.fund/)

### Funding the Web – From Cartel to Covenant (May 2026)

Browser engines are (open) critical infrastructure for five billion people, sustained by a little-known search levy worth hundreds of billions annually — yet governed by no one accountable to the public. Robin Berjon's [recent report](https://infrastructureinsights.fund/projects/browser-funding/), funded by the Digital Infrastructure Insights Fund, diagnoses how this levy mechanically produces a Google search monopoly, defunds the broader web, and leaves the architecture of our shared information space in private hands. To counteract this development, he proposes the Web Infrastructure Search Endowment (WISE) - a multistakeholder institution that would place the existing levy under democratic governance, restructuring it from cartel to covenant. → [Read more](https://ftw.fund/)

### Modeling Dependency-Propagated Ecosystem Impact of Changes in Maintenance Activities: Evaluating Support Strategies in the PyPI Network (8 May 2026)

Open source software ecosystems exhibit dense dependency networks in which maintenance degradation of structurally central packages can propagate widely. Despite increasing attention to open source sustainability, existing support mechanisms lack an explicit, dependency-aware notion of ecosystem-level impact to guide support decisions. In this paper, we introduce a dependency-aware model of ecosystem impact that captures how changes in maintenance activities propagate through the Python Package Index (PyPI) ecosystem and affect its overall state. → [Read more](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06164)

### Open and Closed: The Pursuit of Frontier Models (15 May 2026)

Closed models are setting the pace of innovation, and constantly breaking new ground from a capabilities standpoint. However, Open weights are chasing them, and the cycle times seem to be getting shorter. There are no clear capability moats, and what is frontier today is table stakes tomorrow. → [Read more](https://redmonk.com/sogrady/2026/05/15/open-ai-models/)

## Opportunities and Tenders

## OSHF seeking Program Manager (May 2026)

The Open Science Hardware Foundation is expanding and searching for a new member of our team to fill the role of Program Manager.

## AAIF Ambassador Program (June 2026)

The AAIF Ambassador Program launches with an initial cohort of 10 ambassadors. The goal is project-based advocacy that creates real developer education, community visibility, and adoption pathways for AAIF projects

## Call For Proposals (CFP) - AGNTCon + MCPCon North America (June 2026)

The event brings together the developers, researchers, platform builders, and enterprises advancing the next generation of AI agents—from core agent architectures and infrastructure to the protocols and tools that make agent systems interoperable.

## Applications are open for the ITU Academy online course: Accelerating digital public infrastructure with safeguards (June 2026)

With DPI emerging as a leading approach to inclusive national digital transformation, this course equips government implementers and digital practitioners with a Safeguards-by-Design framework to build trusted and resilient systems built on reusable components, interoperable standards, and open architectures.

## IMPAC3T-IP™ Academy certified training (June 2026)

The IMPAC3T-IP™ Academy offers a certified and subsidised training programme to introduce the IMPAC3T-IP Toolbox and to offer the opportunity to become a certified toolbox user.

## Vacancy: Open-Source Evangelist at G-Research (June 2026)

This role acts as the connective tissue between the internal engineering world of G-Research and the external universe of open-source software.

# OTR 通訊 #3：形塑開放轉型：OTR 研討會 6 月 9 日說明會

我們達成了開放技術研究（Open Technology Research，簡稱 OTR）的另一個里程碑。

本週，OTR [發表](https://opentechresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Open-Technology-Research-A-Shared-Research-Agenda.pdf)了其共同研究議程——這是一份刻意公開的草案，指出了我們在理解、衡量與維持開放技術方面最關鍵的落差——並正式啟動了 [OTR 2026 研討會](https://symposium.opentechresearch.org/)（將於 10 月 26 日至 27 日在[巴塞隆納大學](https://web.ub.edu/en/)舉行）的[徵件](https://pretalx.com/otrsymposium2026/cfp)。我們也歡迎[數位基礎設施洞察基金](https://infrastructureinsights.fund/)（Digital Infrastructure Insights Fund，簡稱 D//F）成為正式合作夥伴，為我們帶來豐富的受資助研究與實作洞察，這將直接推動 OTR 正在努力建構的目標。

此研究議程反映了我們在全球諮詢中一致聽到的心聲：用於開放技術投資、監管與採用的證據基礎仍然破碎、資金不足，且向少數高所得國家傾斜。它指出了最重要的關鍵問題；例如，如何以採購人員和預算單位能夠理解的語言來衡量經濟價值、混合治理模式在實務上如何運作、是什麼讓開放技術的部署得以持久而非可逆，以及我們如何支持維護者與社群——他們正是支撐著全球其他地區所仰賴之基礎設施的基石。這是一份草案，因為我們希望聽到您的反對意見與回饋。

OTR 2026 研討會的主題——形塑開放轉型（Shaping the Open Transition）——反映了焦點的刻意轉移：從梳理問題，轉向探討如何走得更遠。主題演講將立足於已經行之有效的實踐。分組會議旨在將研究與政策及實務直接連結。其目標並非呈現既有的結論，而是作為一個真正的「工作會議」，來凝聚優先事項、提出最緊迫的研究設計，並加強該領域目前所缺乏的跨國連結。

若您的工作涉及開放技術與治理、經濟、永續性、資安、人工智慧（AI）或數位主權的交會點，我們非常期待您的參與。請於 7 月 5 日前[提交](https://pretalx.com/otrsymposium2026/cfp)您的徵件提案。

若您想在投稿前了解更多資訊或與 OTR 社群建立聯繫，歡迎[參加我們即將舉辦的線上說明會](https://opentechresearch.org/blog/got-questions-about-the-otr-symposium-2026-join-our-info-sessions-on-9-june/)。

## 最新開放技術新聞

**開源 AI 硬體或能削弱科技巨頭對 AI 的壟斷 (2026 年 3 月)** – 耗資 4 億美元的公共利益倡議計畫「Current AI」推出了一款與印度 Bhashini 計畫合作開發的開源、離線 AI 裝置。該裝置可在有限的硬體上於本地運行，並支援 22 種印度語言，旨在作為依賴雲端的科技巨頭 AI 的直接替代方案。這是「簡約 AI」（frugal AI）論點的具體實例：追求越來越大的模型只服務了世界上的一部分人，而開放、可攜式且在本地運行的系統可能更適合服務其他地區。→ [閱讀更多](https://restofworld.org/2026/current-ai-bhashini-open-source-handheld-device-2/)

**聯合國推出 Open Source United 入口網站 (2026 年 4 月)** – 聯合國推出了 Open Source United (OSU) 入口網站，作為整個聯合國系統內開源活動的集中參考點。→ [閱讀更多](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/open-source-observatory-osor/news/united-nations-launches-open-source-united-portal)

**使研究與創新資金對齊數位公地動態 (2026 年 4 月)** – 歐盟的研究資金架構是為了短期、市場驅動的創新而建，而非維護和治理讓開源基礎設施得以存續的工作，這導致關鍵的數位公地（Digital Commons）長期面臨資金不足的困境。來自 Open Future 的這份簡報提出了一個分層的解決方案：為基礎開源項目提供持續的核心資金（類似於歐盟主權技術基金），並搭配分級管道以協助成功的公地倡議超越試點階段並擴大編制。→ [閱讀更多](https://openfuture.eu/publication/aligning-research-and-innovation-funding-to-the-dynamics-of-digital-commons/)

**開源組織對美國年齡驗證政策發表意見 (2026 年 5 月)** – 開源促進會（OSI）、Apereo 基金會、FreeBSD 基金會和開源技術改善基金會（OSTIF）發表聯合聲明，要求美國決策者在考慮作業系統的年齡驗證要求時，應與開源社群進行交流。→ [閱讀更多](https://opensource.org/?p=411160)

## 最新開放技術報告與研究

### 評估年齡驗證技術：有效性、副作用與接受度 (2026 年 3 月 26 日)

本文概述並評估了不同類型的年齡驗證技術（Age Assurance Technologies，簡稱 AAT）。它描述並分析了：1）不同的線上年齡驗證方法（年齡驗證、年齡估算、年齡推斷，以及家長控制與同意），以及 2）不同的年齡驗證架構（線上、基於離線裝置、基於離線憑證），並評估了它們的各種組合在 a) 有效性、b) 副作用 和 c) 接受度方面的表現。→ [閱讀更多](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.25695)

### 開放的辯論：治理、權力與網際網路開放性的極限 (2026 年 4 月)

本書是一部編輯合集，探討「網際網路開放性」如何從植根於開放協定的技術理想，轉變為受國家、企業和相互競爭的監管體制所形塑的、充滿爭議的政治與經濟狀態。其核心問題不再是網際網路在原則上是否開放，而是誰有權定義開放，以及當他們定義開放時，由誰來承擔成本。→ [閱讀更多](https://cadmus.eui.eu/entities/publication/a8189891-83f0-43d3-812e-37340cc063a5?ref=internet.exchangepoint.tech)

### 全球技術轉向與創新對人道救援與發展的影響：關於永續發展路徑的系統性回顧 (2026 年 4 月 1 日)

本研究探討人道主義技術（HT）如何重塑全球永續發展（SD）的路徑。它藉由強調創新在促進人類與地球福祉方面的變革潛力，探索了人道主義技術、現有永續發展框架與全球公平之間的關鍵交會點。本研究採用 PRISMA 指南，系統性地評估了 2015 年至 2024 年間以人為本的技術如何有助於實現聯合國的永續發展目標（SDGs），同時指出影響全球永續發展成果的趨勢、差異和政策影響。→ [閱讀更多](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2590291126003086)

### 超越採用：探討行為準則在開源社群中的演變與影響 (2026 年 4 月 15 日)

一項針對數千個 GitHub 專案的行為準則（Codes of Conduct，簡稱 CoC）追蹤研究發現，隨著時間推移，採用行為準則能穩定地吸引新的貢獻者——這是開源社群健康的一個重要訊號。然而，隱憂在於：既有的貢獻者在短期內參與度會降低，這表明行為準則雖以獎勵包容的方式改變了社群文化，但這需要謹慎的變革管理。→ [閱讀更多](https://ftw.fund/)

### 資助網路——從壟斷聯盟到公約 (2026 年 5 月)

瀏覽器引擎是 50 億人所使用（開放）的關鍵基礎設施，由每年價值數千億、鮮為人知的搜尋稅（search levy）所維持——然而，卻沒有任何對公眾負責的人來治理它。由數位基礎設施洞察基金資助的 Robin Berjon [最新報告](https://infrastructureinsights.fund/projects/browser-funding/)，診斷了這種稅收如何機制性地產生 Google 搜尋壟斷、抽走更廣泛網路的資金，並將我們共享的資訊空間架構留給私營機構。為了應對這一發展，他提出了「網路基礎設施搜尋基金」（Web Infrastructure Search Endowment，簡稱 WISE）——一個多方關係人機構，將現有的稅收置於民主治理之下，將其從壟斷聯盟重組為公約。→ [閱讀更多](https://ftw.fund/)

### 模擬維護活動變化對依賴關係傳播之生態系統影響：評估 PyPI 網路中的支持策略 (2026 年 5 月 8 日)

開源軟體生態系統呈現出密集的依賴網路，其中處於結構核心地位的套件其維護品質下降時，影響會廣泛傳播。儘管人們越來越關注開源的永續性，但現有的支持機制仍缺乏明確的、具依賴感知能力的生態系統級影響概念來引導支持決策。在本文中，我們提出了一個具依賴感知的生態系統影響模型，該模型捕捉了維護活動的變化如何在 Python 套件索引（PyPI）生態系統中傳播並影響其整體狀態。→ [閱讀更多](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06164)

### 開源與閉源：前沿模型的追逐 (2026 年 5 月 15 日)

閉源模型正在主導創新的步伐，並從能力角度不斷開拓新領域。然而，開源權重模型正緊追其後，且追趕的週期似乎正在變短。目前沒有明顯的能力護城河，今天的前沿可能就是明天的基本配備。→ [閱讀更多](https://redmonk.com/sogrady/2026/05/15/open-ai-models/)

## 機會與招標

## OSHF 徵求專案經理 (2026 年 5 月)

開放科學硬體基金會（Open Science Hardware Foundation，簡稱 OSHF）正在擴編，並尋找新的團隊成員來擔任專案經理（Program Manager）一職。

## AAIF 大使計劃 (2026 年 6 月)

AAIF 大使計劃正式啟動，首批招募了 10 位大使。其目標是透過專案導向的推廣，為 AAIF 專案提供真正的開發者教育、社群曝光度以及採用路徑。

## 徵件啟動 (CFP) - AGNTCon + MCPCon 北美 (2026 年 6 月)

本活動匯聚了推動下一代 AI 代理人（AI agents）發展的開發者、研究人員、平台建構者和企業——從核心代理人架構與基礎設施，到使代理人系統具備互操作性的協定與工具。

## 國際電信聯盟學院線上課程開放申請：以安全保障加速數位公共基礎設施建設 (2026 年 6 月)

隨著數位公共基礎設施（DPI）成為推動包容性國家數位轉型的主流方法，本課程為政府執行人員 and 數位從業者提供「設計安全保障」（Safeguards-by-Design）框架，以建構基於可重複使用元件、互操作標準和開放架構之值得信賴且具韌性的系統。

## IMPAC3T-IP™ 學院認證培訓 (2026 年 6 月)

IMPAC3T-IP™ 學院提供一項獲得認證且受補助的培訓計劃，旨在介紹 IMPAC3T-IP 工具箱，並提供成為認證工具箱使用者的機會。

## 職缺：G-Research 開源佈道師 (2026 年 6 月)

此職缺將作為 G-Research 內部工程領域與外部開源軟體世界之間的連結橋樑。

# OTR 通訊 #3：形塑開放轉型：OTR 研討會 6 月 9 日說明會

我們達成了開放技術研究（Open Technology Research，簡稱 OTR）的另一個里程碑。

本週，OTR [發表](https://opentechresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Open-Technology-Research-A-Shared-Research-Agenda.pdf)了其共同研究議程——這是一份刻意公開的草案，指出了我們在理解、衡量與維持開放技術方面最關鍵的落差——並正式啟動了 [OTR 2026 研討會](https://symposium.opentechresearch.org/)（將於 10 月 26 日至 27 日在[巴塞隆納大學](https://web.ub.edu/en/)舉行）的[徵件](https://pretalx.com/otrsymposium2026/cfp)。我們也歡迎[數位基礎設施洞察基金](https://infrastructureinsights.fund/)（Digital Infrastructure Insights Fund，簡稱 D//F）成為正式合作夥伴，為我們帶來豐富的受資助研究與實作洞察，這將直接推動 OTR 正在努力建構的目標。

此研究議程反映了我們在全球諮詢中一致聽到的心聲：用於開放技術投資、監管與採用的證據基礎仍然破碎、資金不足，且向少數高所得國家傾斜。它指出了最重要的關鍵問題；例如，如何以採購人員和預算單位能夠理解的語言來衡量經濟價值、混合治理模式在實務上如何運作、是什麼讓開放技術的部署得以持久而非可逆，以及我們如何支持維護者與社群——他們正是支撐著全球其他地區所仰賴之基礎設施的基石。這是一份草案，因為我們希望聽到您的反對意見與回饋。

OTR 2026 研討會的主題——形塑開放轉型（Shaping the Open Transition）——反映了焦點的刻意轉移：從梳理問題，轉向探討如何走得更遠。主題演講將立足於已經行之有效的實踐。分組會議旨在將研究與政策及實務直接連結。其目標並非呈現既有的結論，而是作為一個真正的「工作會議」，來凝聚優先事項、提出最緊迫的研究設計，並加強該領域目前所缺乏的跨國連結。

若您的工作涉及開放技術與治理、經濟、永續性、資安、人工智慧（AI）或數位主權的交會點，我們非常期待您的參與。請於 7 月 5 日前[提交](https://pretalx.com/otrsymposium2026/cfp)您的徵件提案。

若您想在投稿前了解更多資訊或與 OTR 社群建立聯繫，歡迎[參加我們即將舉辦的線上說明會](https://opentechresearch.org/blog/got-questions-about-the-otr-symposium-2026-join-our-info-sessions-on-9-june/)。

**全球數位公共基礎設施 (DPI) 峰會將於 2027 年在印尼舉辦 (2026 年 5 月)** – 全球 DPI 峰會將於 2027 年 3 月在峇里島舉行——這是其首次在亞洲舉辦——這既反映了印尼在 DPI 領域日益增長的領導地位，也反映了目前已在 100 多個國家啟用的基礎數位系統背後不斷擴大的全球動能。隨著關於 DPI 是建構在開放、可重複使用、互操作的基礎上，還是成為另一層專有鎖定的爭論日益激烈，這是一個非常及時的交流場所。→ [閱讀更多](https://www.undp.org/digital-innovation/press-releases/global-digital-public-infrastructure-dpi-summit-heads-indonesia-2027)

**針對公共從業人員的開源軟體指南 (2026 年 5 月)** – 一份由聯合國開發計劃署（UNDP）支持的開源軟體入門指南，以千里達及托巴哥新成立的開源專案辦公室為主要案例，論證了在小島嶼開發中國家採用開源軟體（OSS）的可行性。其核心論點既具實踐性也具哲學意義：對於預算有限且需要具適應性、互操作性數位基礎設施的政府而言，開源不僅是一項節省成本的措施，更是一項主權策略。→ [閱讀更多](https://www.undp.org/trinidad-and-tobago/blog/open-source-software-public-practitioners)

## 最新開放技術報告與研究

### 評估年齡驗證技術：有效性、副作用與接受度 (2026 年 3 月 26 日)

本文概述並評估了不同類型的年齡驗證技術（Age Assurance Technologies，簡稱 AAT）。它描述並分析了：1）不同的線上年齡驗證方法（年齡驗證、年齡估算、年齡推斷，以及家長控制與同意），以及 2）不同的年齡驗證架構（線上、基於離線裝置、基於離線憑證），並評估了它們的各種組合在 a) 有效性、b) 副作用 和 c) 接受度方面的表現。→ [閱讀更多](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.25695)

### 開放的辯論：治理、權力與網際網路開放性的極限 (2026 年 4 月)

本書是一部編輯合集，探討「網際網路開放性」如何從植根於開放協定的技術理想，轉變為受國家、企業和相互競爭的監管體制所形塑的、充滿爭議的政治與經濟狀態。其核心問題不再是網際網路在原則上是否開放，而是誰有權定義開放，以及當他們定義開放時，由誰來承擔成本。→ [閱讀更多](https://cadmus.eui.eu/entities/publication/a8189891-83f0-43d3-812e-37340cc063a5?ref=internet.exchangepoint.tech)

### 全球技術轉向與創新對人道救援與發展的影響：關於永續發展路徑的系統性回顧 (2026 年 4 月 1 日)

本研究探討人道主義技術（HT）如何重塑全球永續發展（SD）的路徑。它藉由強調創新在促進人類與地球福祉方面的變革潛力，探索了人道主義技術、現有永續發展框架與全球公平之間的關鍵交會點。本研究採用 PRISMA 指南，系統性地評估了 2015 年至 2024 年間以人為本的技術如何有助於實現聯合國的永續發展目標（SDGs），同時指出影響全球永續發展成果的趨勢、差異和政策影響。→ [閱讀更多](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2590291126003086)

### 超越採用：探討行為準則在開源社群中的演變與影響 (2026 年 4 月 15 日)

一項針對數千個 GitHub 專案的行為準則（Codes of Conduct，簡稱 CoC）追蹤研究發現，隨著時間推移，採用行為準則能穩定地吸引新的貢獻者——這是開源社群健康的一個重要訊號。然而，隱憂在於：既有的貢獻者在短期內參與度會降低，這表明行為準則雖以獎勵包容的方式改變了社群文化，但這需要謹慎的變革管理。→ [閱讀更多](https://ftw.fund/)

### 資助網路——從壟斷聯盟到公約 (2026 年 5 月)

瀏覽器引擎是 50 億人所使用（開放）的關鍵基礎設施，由每年價值數千億、鮮為人知的搜尋稅（search levy）所維持——然而，卻沒有任何對公眾負責的人來治理它。由數位基礎設施洞察基金資助的 Robin Berjon [最新報告](https://infrastructureinsights.fund/projects/browser-funding/)，診斷了這種稅收如何機制性地產生 Google 搜尋壟斷、抽走更廣泛網路的資金，並將我們共享的資訊空間架構留給私營機構。為了應對這一發展，他提出了「網路基礎設施搜尋基金」（Web Infrastructure Search Endowment，簡稱 WISE）——一個多方關係人機構，將現有的稅收置於民主治理之下，將其從壟斷聯盟重組為公約。→ [閱讀更多](https://ftw.fund/)

### 模擬維護活動變化對依賴關係傳播之生態系統影響：評估 PyPI 網路中的支持策略 (2026 年 5 月 8 日)

開源軟體生態系統呈現出密集的依賴網路，其中處於結構核心地位的套件其維護品質下降時，影響會廣泛傳播。儘管人們越來越關注開源的永續性，但現有的支持機制仍缺乏明確的、具依賴感知能力的生態系統級影響概念來引導支持決策。在本文中，我們提出了一個具依賴感知的生態系統影響模型，該模型捕捉了維護活動的變化如何在 Python 套件索引（PyPI）生態系統中傳播並影響其整體狀態。→ [閱讀更多](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06164)

### 開源與閉源：前沿模型的追逐 (2026 年 5 月 15 日)

閉源模型正在主導創新的步伐，並從能力角度不斷開拓新領域。然而，開源權重模型正緊追其後，且追趕的週期似乎正在變短。目前沒有明顯的能力護城河，今天的前沿可能就是明天的基本配備。→ [閱讀更多](https://redmonk.com/sogrady/2026/05/15/open-ai-models/)
